metadata.description: Public half of the SSH key pair used for the break-glass local administrator. Generate one with: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/librechat -C librechat-admin. Day-to-day access should use Entra ID instead ("az ssh vm"); this key is what gets you in when that is broken.

Source addresses allowed to reach SSH (port 22), in CIDR form, e.g. ["203.0.113.4/32"]. Find yours with: curl -fsS https://api.ipify.org. ⚠️ A home broadband address usually changes without warning. If it changes you are locked out — recovery is Azure Portal > this NSG > edit the ssh rule, which takes about a minute and needs no SSH. Read docs/troubleshooting.md#locked-out-of-ssh BEFORE you need it.
Address that receives every monitoring alert. Use one a person actually reads.

Prefix for every resource name. "librechat" produces vm-librechat-prod, nsg-librechat-prod, and so on. (The key vault and storage account additionally carry a uniqueness suffix, because their names are globally unique across all of Azure.)
Environment suffix, used in resource names.
Azure region. Defaults to the resource group's region.
Availability zone. Pinning the VM and its disks to one zone is required for them to be attachable to each other.
Virtual machine size. 4 vCPU / 16 GB comfortably runs the whole stack for a few hundred users. See docs/cost-model.md before changing it.
Local administrator account name for the virtual machine.
Size of the data disk in GB. Everything that must survive an OS rebuild lives here: databases, uploaded files, letterheads, backups.
Data disk performance tier.
Repository that this machine deploys from. It must be public, or the VM will need credentials it does not have.
Branch to deploy.
Create daily whole-machine backups with 30-day retention. The only thing that restores uploaded files.
Public URL of the health endpoint to monitor, e.g. https://chat.example.org/api/health. Leave empty until DNS points at this machine; the availability test is skipped while it is empty.
Run the five-minute deploy timer on this machine. Set false where deploys are triggered by a pipeline instead, so a timer run cannot race it.

Where the data disk is mounted. ⚠️ This must match DATA_DIR in env.defaults — cloud-init mounts the disk here and the containers bind-mount from there. .github/workflows/validate.yml asserts the two agree.
Tags applied to every resource.

variables.$fxv#0:
#cloud-config
# =============================================================================
# First-boot setup for the LibreChat virtual machine.
# =============================================================================
# Runs once, automatically, the first time the machine starts. It prepares the
# host and stops: Docker, the data disk, a checkout of the deployment
# repository, and the timers that keep it up to date.
#
# It deliberately does NOT start the application. At this point in the story
# there are no secrets in the key vault yet, so a stack started here would come
# up misconfigured and have to be repaired rather than simply started. The first
# real deploy is a decision you make once your secrets exist:
#
#     sudo /srv/librechat/app/scripts/deploy.sh --force
#
# The __PLACEHOLDERS__ below are substituted by infra/main.bicep at deployment
# time. Editing this file by hand on a running machine has no effect — it is
# consumed once, at first boot.
#
# To see what happened here:  sudo cloud-init status --long
#                             sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
# =============================================================================

package_update: true
package_upgrade: true

packages:
  - ca-certificates
  - curl
  - gnupg
  - git
  - jq
  - util-linux      # flock, mountpoint — both used by deploy.sh
  - unattended-upgrades

write_files:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Per-machine settings.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The one thing that cannot come from the key vault is which key vault to use.
  - path: /etc/librechat-deploy.conf
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      # Read by scripts/deploy.sh, scripts/render-env.sh and the bootstrap
      # script. Written once by cloud-init; safe to edit if the vault is ever
      # renamed or the repository moves.
      KV_NAME=__KEY_VAULT_NAME__
      DEPLOY_BRANCH=__REPO_BRANCH__
      REPO_URL=__REPO_URL__

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Bootstrap: get the repository onto this machine.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Separate from deploy.sh because deploy.sh lives INSIDE the repository and so
  # cannot be the thing that fetches it.
  #
  # Re-runnable, and expected to be re-run. cloud-init calls it once at first
  # boot, which may well be before the key vault has been seeded — the vault is
  # created by the same deployment as this machine, so at first boot it is
  # usually still empty. A failure here is not a problem; run it again once your
  # secrets exist:
  #
  #     sudo /usr/local/sbin/librechat-bootstrap.sh
  - path: /usr/local/sbin/librechat-bootstrap.sh
    permissions: '0750'
    content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      set -euo pipefail

      . /etc/librechat-deploy.conf

      echo "[bootstrap] repository: $REPO_URL ($DEPLOY_BRANCH)"

      az account show >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
        az login --identity --allow-no-subscriptions --output none

      # --- A read-only deploy key, if this repository is private -------------
      # A public repository needs no credential at all, which is the whole point
      # of publishing it — a grantee's machine clones with nothing configured.
      # While the repository is still private, a read-only deploy key bridges
      # the gap. It is stored base64-encoded because a .env-style secret cannot
      # hold a multi-line value, and it is named BOOTSTRAP-* so render-env.sh
      # keeps it out of the application's environment entirely.
      #
      # When the repository becomes public: delete the secret, delete the deploy
      # key on GitHub, and change REPO_URL here to the https:// form.
      if key_b64=$(az keyvault secret show --vault-name "$KV_NAME" \
                     --name BOOTSTRAP-GIT-DEPLOY-KEY --query value -o tsv 2>/dev/null); then
        echo "[bootstrap] installing the read-only deploy key"
        install -d -m 0700 /root/.ssh
        printf '%s' "$key_b64" | base64 -d > /root/.ssh/id_ed25519
        chmod 0600 /root/.ssh/id_ed25519
        ssh-keyscan -t rsa,ecdsa,ed25519 github.com > /root/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null
        chmod 0644 /root/.ssh/known_hosts
      else
        echo "[bootstrap] no deploy key in the vault — assuming a public repository"
      fi

      # --- Clone, or leave an existing checkout alone ------------------------
      if [ -d /srv/librechat/app/.git ]; then
        echo "[bootstrap] already cloned; leaving it to deploy.sh"
      else
        mkdir -p /srv/librechat
        git clone --branch "$DEPLOY_BRANCH" --depth 1 "$REPO_URL" /srv/librechat/app
        echo "[bootstrap] cloned"
      fi

      git config --global --add safe.directory /srv/librechat/app
      chmod +x /srv/librechat/app/scripts/*.sh

      echo "[bootstrap] done — next: /srv/librechat/app/scripts/deploy.sh --force"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The deploy timer — the entire autodeploy configuration.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Once the repository is public, `git pull` needs no credentials at all —
  # nothing to configure, rotate, or leak. (While it is still private, the
  # read-only deploy key installed by librechat-bootstrap.sh stands in.) A run
  # where nothing has changed costs one request, which is what makes a
  # five-minute interval reasonable.
  - path: /etc/systemd/system/librechat-deploy.service
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=Deploy LibreChat from the repository
      After=docker.service network-online.target
      Requires=docker.service
      Wants=network-online.target

      [Service]
      Type=oneshot
      WorkingDirectory=/srv/librechat/app
      ExecStart=/srv/librechat/app/scripts/deploy.sh
      # Deploys pull images and wait on health checks; the default 90s would cut
      # a legitimate first deploy short and leave the stack half-started.
      TimeoutStartSec=1800
      StandardOutput=journal
      StandardError=journal

  - path: /etc/systemd/system/librechat-deploy.timer
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=Check for new LibreChat deployments every five minutes

      [Timer]
      OnBootSec=5min
      OnUnitActiveSec=5min
      # Spread load and avoid every machine in a fleet fetching simultaneously.
      RandomizedDelaySec=60s
      Unit=librechat-deploy.service

      [Install]
      WantedBy=timers.target

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The nightly database dump.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - path: /etc/systemd/system/librechat-backup.service
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=Dump the LibreChat database to Azure Blob Storage
      After=docker.service
      Requires=docker.service

      [Service]
      Type=oneshot
      WorkingDirectory=/srv/librechat/app
      ExecStart=/srv/librechat/app/scripts/backup-mongo.sh
      TimeoutStartSec=3600
      StandardOutput=journal
      StandardError=journal

  - path: /etc/systemd/system/librechat-backup.timer
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=Nightly LibreChat database dump

      [Timer]
      OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:17:00 UTC
      # Catch up after the machine has been off, rather than silently skipping a
      # night's backup.
      Persistent=true
      RandomizedDelaySec=300
      Unit=librechat-backup.service

      [Install]
      WantedBy=timers.target

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Unattended security updates.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Security patches only, and never an automatic reboot — a reboot chosen by
  # the machine at 6am is a reboot nobody is watching. Reboot deliberately when
  # /var/run/reboot-required appears.
  - path: /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/52-librechat-unattended
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot "false";
      Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Kernel-Packages "true";
      Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Dependencies "true";

runcmd:
  # ===========================================================================
  # 1. Docker, from Docker's own repository.
  # ===========================================================================
  # Not the distribution package: Ubuntu's docker.io lags well behind and does
  # not ship the Compose v2 plugin this deployment uses.
  - install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
  - curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  - chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  - >-
      echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc]
      https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable"
      > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list
  - apt-get update
  - DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
  - systemctl enable --now docker

  # ===========================================================================
  # 2. Azure CLI, for reading secrets with the machine's own identity.
  # ===========================================================================
  - curl -fsSL https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
  - chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
  - >-
      echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg]
      https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli/ $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") main"
      > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli.list
  - apt-get update
  - DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y azure-cli

  # ===========================================================================
  # 3. yq, for merging the storage overlay into librechat.yaml.
  # ===========================================================================
  # Ubuntu's `yq` package is a different program with different syntax. This is
  # mikefarah/yq, which is what scripts/deploy.sh is written against.
  - curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/yq "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.44.3/yq_linux_amd64"
  - chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/yq
  - /usr/local/bin/yq --version

  # ===========================================================================
  # 4. The data disk.
  # ===========================================================================
  # Everything that must outlive the operating system lives here: databases,
  # uploaded files, letterheads, certificates, backups.
  #
  # Mounted by UUID, never by device name. Device names are assigned in the
  # order the kernel happens to enumerate disks, so /dev/sdc can become /dev/sdd
  # after a resize or a reboot — at which point the machine boots with the wrong
  # filesystem mounted, or none at all. The UUID belongs to the filesystem and
  # does not move.
  - |
    set -eux
    DEVICE=/dev/disk/azure/scsi1/lun0
    MOUNT=__DATA_DIR__

    # Wait for the disk to be attached and visible.
    for _ in $(seq 1 30); do [ -e "$DEVICE" ] && break; sleep 2; done
    [ -e "$DEVICE" ] || { echo "data disk never appeared at $DEVICE"; exit 1; }

    # Format only if there is no filesystem. This is what makes reattaching an
    # existing data disk to a rebuilt machine safe rather than catastrophic.
    if ! blkid "$DEVICE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mkfs.ext4 -L librechat-data "$DEVICE"
    fi

    UUID=$(blkid -s UUID -o value "$DEVICE")
    mkdir -p "$MOUNT"
    grep -q "$UUID" /etc/fstab || \
      echo "UUID=$UUID $MOUNT ext4 defaults,nofail,discard 0 2" >> /etc/fstab
    mount -a
    mountpoint -q "$MOUNT"

  # ===========================================================================
  # 5. Directories on the data disk.
  # ===========================================================================
  # The database images start as root and chown their own data directories, so
  # those need no ownership setup. The LibreChat container does not — it runs as
  # uid 1000 and will fail to write uploads into a root-owned directory, with an
  # EACCES buried in its logs and no other symptom.
  - |
    set -eux
    MOUNT=__DATA_DIR__
    mkdir -p "$MOUNT"/{mongo,meili_data_v1.35.1,pgvector,uploads,images,logs,skill,letterheads,caddy/data,caddy/config,backups,migrations}
    chown -R 1000:1000 "$MOUNT"/uploads "$MOUNT"/images "$MOUNT"/logs "$MOUNT"/skill
    chmod 0755 "$MOUNT"/letterheads

  # ===========================================================================
  # 6. The deployment repository.
  # ===========================================================================
  # Attempted once, and allowed to fail. The key vault is created by the same
  # deployment as this machine, so at first boot it is usually still empty — and
  # a private repository needs a deploy key from it. Re-run after seeding:
  #
  #     sudo /usr/local/sbin/librechat-bootstrap.sh
  #
  # For a public repository this succeeds first time and there is nothing to do.
  - /usr/local/sbin/librechat-bootstrap.sh || echo "bootstrap deferred — re-run it once the key vault is seeded"

  # ===========================================================================
  # 7. Timers.
  # ===========================================================================
  # Enabled but not started. Nothing deploys until a human runs the first deploy
  # by hand, once the key vault has been seeded.
  - systemctl daemon-reload
  - systemctl enable librechat-backup.timer
  - |
    if [ "__DEPLOY_TIMER_ENABLED__" = "true" ]; then
      systemctl enable librechat-deploy.timer
      echo "deploy timer enabled; it will begin after the first manual deploy"
    else
      systemctl disable librechat-deploy.timer || true
      echo "deploy timer disabled — deploys are expected to come from a pipeline"
    fi

final_message: |
  ==========================================================================
  Host ready. The application is NOT running yet — that is expected.

  Next:
    1. Put your secrets in the key vault named in /etc/librechat-deploy.conf
       (see .env.example for the catalogue and the dash-to-underscore rule).
    2. Point DNS at this machine's public address.
    3. sudo /usr/local/sbin/librechat-bootstrap.sh
       (fetches the repository; harmless to re-run, and usually necessary
        because the vault was still empty when this machine first booted)
    4. sudo /srv/librechat/app/scripts/deploy.sh --force

  Then the five-minute timer keeps it up to date on its own.
  ==========================================================================

metricAlerts.name: cpu-high
metricAlerts.description: Sustained high CPU. Usually a runaway container or genuine load growth.

metricAlerts.name: memory-low
metricAlerts.description: Available memory is nearly exhausted. The kernel will start killing containers.

metricAlerts.name: network-out-high
metricAlerts.description: Unusual outbound traffic. Worth a look — this is what data exfiltration looks like.

metricAlerts.name: os-disk-iops-high
metricAlerts.description: The OS disk is at its throughput limit and everything on it is now slow.

metricAlerts.name: data-disk-iops-high
metricAlerts.description: The data disk is at its throughput limit. The databases live here.

metricAlerts.name: vm-unavailable
metricAlerts.description: Azure reports the virtual machine itself as unavailable.

Name of the key vault holding this deployment's secrets.
Name of the storage account holding nightly database dumps.
Point your DNS A records at this address.

Set BACKUP_STORAGE_ACCOUNT to this in Key Vault.
